raw.title: Senior Director, People & Culture
raw.description:
Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it.  Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.

We work with over 5,000+ teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT BUILDING LEADERS, SHAPING CULTURE, AND ENABLING BUSINESS SUCCESS

The Senior Director, People & Culture is a pivotal senior role within our London Office and a key member of Catapult's global P&C leadership team. Working three days in the office and partnering closely with senior business leaders, you will drive strategic impact while shaping both the culture and operational effectiveness of the EMEA region.

Reporting to the Vice President, People & Culture, based in Melbourne, you will lead an in-region team of three and be responsible for designing and implementing strategies that enable, engage, develop and retain exceptional talent.

Success in this role requires a balance of strategic thinking and practical execution. You will thrive in a fast-paced, global environment and be energised by creating innovative, scalable solutions that strengthen leadership capability and foster a high-performance culture across the region.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Develop and execute strategic workforce plans, coaching senior leaders on organisational design, change management, communication, and talent development to drive engagement, retention, and business performance.
  • Shape culture and values by identifying organisational needs and implementing impactful, scalable people solutions.
  • Drive a consistent, high-quality employee experience across the EMEA region, spanning three offices, 16 countries, and multiple employment frameworks.
  • Provide hands-on support and strategic partnership to leaders, teams, and employees, ensuring people strategies are aligned with business goals.
  • Partner with the Talent team to deliver strategic initiatives across learning and development, diversity, equity and inclusion, reward, workforce planning, and talent acquisition.
  • Mentor and lead regional P&C team members, fostering a high-performance culture.
  • Leverage data and insights to identify trends, inform decision-making, and influence strategic outcomes.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • A commercial mindset and the ability to connect people decisions to business outcomes, building credibility and influence with senior leaders across regions and cultures.
  • Significant People & Culture leadership experience in a multi-country EMEA environment, with working knowledge of UK and German employment law.
  • Proven success partnering with senior leaders in a fast-paced, high-growth, global organisation to drive transformation and business outcomes.
  • The ability to balance competing priorities across the employee lifecycle without compromising quality or attention to detail.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and bringing clarity, structure, and momentum to complex challenges.
  • A strategic yet hands-on approach, balancing pace with employee development, engagement, and belonging.
  • Experience designing creative, commercially driven solutions to complex business challenges.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the organisation.
  • High levels of energy, adaptability, and resilience, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • A passion for creating a market-leading employee experience and fostering a high-performance culture.
  • Flexibility to work across global time zones when required.

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months, you have built strong relationships with senior leaders and key stakeholders and are recognised as a trusted P&C partner. You have a clear understanding of workforce opportunities, challenges, and priorities, with a defined view of how P&C can enable business performance. Your direct team is aligned on priorities, ways of working, and expectations, and regional P&C processes are operating with consistency and quality.
  • In 12 months time, you are driving meaningful impact through strategic workforce initiatives, stronger leadership capability, and an enhanced employee experience. Leaders are empowered to navigate people challenges effectively, global P&C initiatives are successfully embedded across teams, and data and insights are being used to inform decisions. You are a valued member of the global P&C leadership team, helping shape and deliver a high-performance culture across Catapult.

 

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet! 

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch! We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.

All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

Location: London (Hybrid)

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer, healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores, giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

Role Purpose

As Legal Counsel, you'll support every part of the company, with a primary focus on day-to-day commercial matters and the scope to advise across a wide range of legal issues.

This is a varied, high-visibility role for a lawyer who wants to take real ownership of day-to-day legal matters, with the backing of a supportive wider Legal team.

A Day in the Life

  • Drafting, reviewing and negotiating a broad range of commercial agreements

  • Giving clear, solution-focused advice to colleagues across the business on their day-to-day legal questions

  • Getting to grips with new and evolving areas of law, and with the diverse needs of our distinct business units

  • Over time, and with the right support, stretching beyond your current experience into areas such as M&A, governance and company law, incentives, employment law, new product and service launches, and expansion into new jurisdictions

Who You Are

Essential

  • An English-qualified (or US-qualified) lawyer with at least one year of post-qualification experience (or equivalent US experience)

  • Proven experience of commercial contracting

  • Versatile, with a genuine team mindset

  • Professional, with high levels of integrity and excellent attention to detail

  • Committed to fostering an inclusive culture within a diverse team

Desirable

  • Training at a leading law firm

  • Some in-house experience, ideally in life sciences, healthcare or a venture-backed scale-up

  • An interest in science and technology

  • Willingness to support the wider Legal team on matters beyond your existing experience

Your Package

We are committed to providing a transparent, supportive, and rewarding work environment.

Compensation & Growth

  • Competitive Reward: Salaries are externally benchmarked annually to ensure market-aligned compensation.

  • Clear Career Path: A straightforward, open progression framework means you'll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal.

  • Continuous Learning: Including external courses and a wide library of L&D materials, because your growth is our success.

Wellbeing & Time Off

  • Holiday: 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, plus an extra 3-day company-wide shutdown at year-end.

  • Financial & Health Security: Robust benefits including a market-leading pension scheme, comprehensive private health insurance for you and your family with NO excess, critical illness, and life assurance.

  • Enhanced Leave: Enhanced paid family leave to support all new parents.

Work Environment & Culture

  • Hybrid Working

raw.title: (Junior) PR & Communications Manager EMEA
raw.description:
At Statista, we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

About the Role

Statista is seeking a (Junior) PR & Communications Manager to support and shape communications activities across the EMEA region, with a clear focus on Germany and the UK. Reporting to the Head of PR & Communications, you will turn Statista’s data, products, and corporate stories into compelling narratives, proactive media relations, and relevant communications content.

This is a hands-on role for a professional at the beginning of their career. You will take ownership of day-to-day PR execution in Germany and the UK while working closely with an international PR & Communications team.

The ideal candidate is a strong writer and proactive communicator who understands what makes a story relevant for journalists, enjoys turning complex topics into clear narratives, and is excited to grow their career in a fast-moving global company.

If you thrive on making things happen and want to make a real impact by empowering people with data to make fact-based decisions, this is your opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute day-to-day PR and communications activities across EMEA, with a clear focus on Germany and the UK – in alignment with business objectives and the global communications strategy.

  • Draft, edit, and tailor communications materials in German and English, including press releases, media pitches, op-eds, expert commentary, media alerts, Q&As, briefing documents, and key messages.

  • Help plan and execute always-on media relations activities to secure earned media coverage across Tier 1 and Tier 2 business, technology, trade, national, and podcast media; including monitoring of industry trends and news developments to identify proactive PR opportunities.

  • Support the planning and execution of integrated communications campaigns, including thought leadership and corporate announcements (e.g., product news, business developments).

  • Build and maintain relationships with journalists, editors and relevant industry influencers across German and UK business, technology, national, and trade media.

  • Help position and prepare executives, industry experts, and researchers for media interviews, speaking engagements, and other external appearances to ensure impactful and consistent representation of Statista across the EMEA region.

  • Create and manage LinkedIn content for executives, translating business priorities, data, and thought-leadership topics into authentic, engaging executive communications.

  • Contribute to PR & communications work beyond the core Germany and UK remit where needed, including support for U.S. PR activities, and media outreach across other EMEA markets.

  • Help manage and coordinate PR-related partnerships and external speaking opportunities

Qualifications

  • 2–3+ years of relevant professional experience in PR, corporate communications, brand communications, journalism, or a related field, gained in-house or at a PR/communications agency.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both German and English.

  • Strong writing and editing skills, with experience producing high-quality press materials, media pitches, and other editorial content for different audiences.

  • Experience in media relations, including pitching stories that resonate with journalists, responding to media requests, and building relationships with journalists and editors.

  • A good understanding of the German media landscape; an initial understanding of the EMEA region, especially the UK media market and existing relationships with UK journalists are a plus.

  • Ability to identify compelling angles and turn complex information, products, and business topics into clear and relevant stories that resonate with media.

  • A proactive, collaborative, and reliable working style, with the confidence to engage constructively with cross-functional stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working within a global organization or agency

  • Experienced in analyzing data and data-led storytelling.

  • Experience supporting executive communications and thought leadership programs.

  • Curiosity about business, technology, AI, and data topics that shape public discussion.

  • Familiarity with AI-enabled communications is a plus.

Why Statista

At Statista, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions through trusted data and insights. Join us in shaping how businesses, organizations, and individuals understand the world through data.

What we offer

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

  • Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

  • Hybrid work and flex-time

  • International team and social events

  • Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

  • Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

  • Career & training opportunities

  • Attractive locations and modern offices

  • Mental health support with OpenUp

Some of the benefits listed here apply only to the German entity and to Junior-level roles or above.

The AI Governance and Control (AIGC) platform understands user / agent intent and data context in real time, giving security teams visibility and control across every tool and workflow so companies can move faster with AI while minimizing risk.

We operate in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech: the emerging intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It's a market still being defined, and we're among the first to build natively for it - protecting sensitive data in real time, at the endpoint, with minimal friction for the teams using it. Enterprises get full visibility and control. Their people get to innovate without guardrails slowing them down.

Named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, Harmonic is gaining serious recognition and serious traction. We're led by deep cybersecurity expertise and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel.

As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. That's what we build.

How We Work: AI-First by Design

Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work, from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity.

For some, this involves tinkering and remaining open to emerging tools; for others, it means architecting entirely new systems with AI at the core. We will be transparent about expectations for every role and provide the tools and support needed for you to thrive.

About the Team

Our Product Delivery team is the engine that turns vision into impact. We ship early and often, getting valuable features into the hands of customers quickly and iterating from there. We work in the open by default, sharing progress and ideas, and we trust each other to own outcomes. We’re a small but mighty crew where every person plays a critical role and we’re committed to using AI to work smarter and faster.

About the Role

We're looking for an AI/ML Product Engineer to build the insight layer of Harmonic: the ML that makes sense of how people and agents are actually using AI, so our customers can see where it's creating value and where it's creating risk.

This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role with real product impact. You'll take problems from messy raw data all the way to a shipped, customer-facing insight, working directly with product, engineering, security and the customers themselves.

This is about turning AI usage into insight that customers act on. Classification and clustering are how we do that today, but you'll choose whatever approach fits the problem. It's Python-first engineering, not notebook analysis.

What You'll Do

  • Turn raw AI usage data into insights customers can see, trust and act on

  • Own insight features end to end, from framing the question with users and product partners through to production and iteration

  • Make sense of unstructured data at scale, with the quality of every output measured and understood

  • Build and maintain the data pipelines behind your models, and own their deployment and reliability in production

  • Build the evaluation frameworks, ground-truth sets and error analysis that prove an insight holds up before a customer sees it

  • Quantify uncertainty and communicate confidence clearly, so the product never presents a shaky signal as a certain one

  • Shape the product surface itself: what the model should show, to whom, and why

  • Keep pace with a fast-moving field, adopting new models and approaches as they prove themselves and retiring the ones that don't

  • Work across a polyglot stack: Python at the core, with Java (Spring Boot) and occasionally TypeScript when the task demands it, deployed on AWS

What You Bring

  • A track record of shipping production ML that customers or downstream product surfaces depend on, such as text or behaviour classifiers, or clustering and embedding pipelines

  • Solid applied ML foundations across supervised classification and unsupervised grouping, with a clear view of which model families you've used and why; this role isn't a fit for a background built mainly on forecasting or time-series prediction

  • Strong production Python for ML and data engineering – code in version control, tested and deployed, not just explored

  • Rigour about validity: you routinely report precision and recall, confidence intervals and baselines, and you've run experiments or human-in-the-loop review to verify automated conclusions

  • Experience delivering ML as part of a product team on a customer-visible surface, ideally having owned an insights, analytics or intelligence feature yourself

  • A quantitative background (statistics, CS, physics, econometrics or equivalent) applied to real data problems

  • Comfort in a polyglot codebase and a willingness to pick up a second language on the job

  • Hybrid in our Shoreditch office around two days a week, potential for Remote for exceptional candidates

You Might Be a Fit if You

  • Have built products in cybersecurity, AI detection, data protection, governance or enterprise SaaS – or have a real interest in how organisations adopt AI safely

  • Have worked on taxonomy design, data labelling, or entity and intent categorisation in a product context

  • Have been an early or founding engineer or data scientist and defined the product surface yourself

  • Care whether a signal in the data is real, and will argue about sampling bias and statistical validity when it matters

  • Have translated messy data into dashboards, scores or narratives that buyers rely on

  • Want a senior IC seat with build-it-yourself scope, not a step onto a management ladder

  • Thrive in early-stage ambiguity and prefer small, fast product companies to large platform teams

  • Leverage AI tools as an engineer to help you build smarter, faster and better

Why Join Us

This isn't just a job - it's a chance to help define a category. Harmonic Security was named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, and we're just getting started. We're building at the intersection of AI and security, carving out an emerging market where the rules haven't been written yet, and the people who join now will write them.

We believe today's talent is tomorrow's success, and we're committed to creating an environment where you can do the best work of your life.

  • Recognized momentum - We made the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, a signal that the market is taking notice

  • Rare market opportunity - Join early in a category-defining company at the convergence of AI and security, where your work directly shapes how enterprises tackle one of the biggest unsolved problems in tech

  • Competitive pay and meaningful equity - A real stake in Harmonic's success, not a token gesture

  • Comprehensive benefits - pension plan and flexible hybrid work

  • A small, high-trust team that values transparency, creativity, and continuous learning - no politics, no bureaucracy

  • Thoughtful leadership - that cares deeply about your growth, not just your output

  • Annual global off-sites - past trips include Lisbon, Portugal and Nashville, TN

  • Real ownership - you'll shape the product, the culture, and the direction of the company from day one

Harmonic's Core Values

🌱 Flourish in the Unknown

We embrace new, unfamiliar situations that require initiative and rapid decision-making. We orient ourselves quickly and deliver results with minimal guidance.

🔥 Never Full

We raise our hands, take on challenges, and assist others whenever possible. We hunger for opportunities to learn and do more.

🤝 Perfect Harmony

We support one another to create cohesion and unity. We collaborate openly, share feedback honestly, and help everyone produce their best work

You'll treat integrations as a product with real users, not just plumbing, and you'll decide which connections matter most and build them well. As Harmonic grows, we expect the scope of the role to grow with it.

What You'll Do

  • Owning our APIs, webhooks, MCP servers and integrations end to end, deciding what gets built, for whom and in what order, and being able to defend that order clearly.

  • Collaborating with our commercial and partnerships teams to understand where integrations and partner opportunities create real value for customers, and translating that into products people use.

  • Deciding which integrations are worth building and which aren't, using your judgement and understanding of our other product areas to determine where the benefits can be felt the most.

  • Holding technical conversations with engineers, both ours and those at partners and customers, covering API design, authentication, and common integration patterns to understand how systems fit together and how they might break.

  • Spending real time with existing customers and prospects, including sales calls and proof-of-value engagements where an integration can make or break a deal, and holding your own in conversations with CISOs, CIOs and their technical teams.

  • Getting hands-on yourself, whether that means calling an API to see how it really behaves, testing a webhook flow end to end, reading a partner's documentation to assess how hard an integration will be, or prototyping to test an idea before more time is committed.

  • Producing work, whether that's discovery, specifications or written thinking, that is clear and technically sound enough to stand up to scrutiny from engineers without needing to be fully rebuilt.

What You'll Bring

You've owned meaningful product work end to end and seen it through to customers, and you can talk not only about what you shipped but about whether it worked and how you knew. You have strong fundamentals to go with that: your writing is clear, your discovery is sound, your prioritisation holds up when someone pushes on it, and you take pride in your quality of work.

You're comfortable being technical. You don't need to write production code, but you're comfortable designing and critiquing APIs, you understand how webhooks, authentication and data flows work in practice, and you can work through detail confidently with engineers. You understand that the people using your products are often developers whose expectations may be very different from those of an end user. You also follow how emerging protocols such as MCP and A2A are changing the way products and AI agents connect, and use this to inform your view of how Harmonic should integrate.

You're also energised by the reality of a startup, where priorities shift, information is incomplete and you'll often need to work out the right approach as you go rather than follow one that already exists.

raw.description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We are looking for a sales engineer to join our sales team and drive the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.

This role bridges the technical and commercial worlds. You'll need interpersonal and technical skills to build relationships with process engineers in cement plants and understand their challenges. Analytical skills will be essential to delve deep into complex plant data and work out how Gigaton's AI products can solve their most critical issues.

Building on that, you'll need strategic thinking and commercial awareness to turn your findings into concise, compelling proposals for decision-makers at our customers, from the C-suite down.

Ultimately, you'll build clarity from uncertainty, making sure we agree a shared roadmap with our customers that puts our solutions on track for significant real-world benefits before a contract is signed.

Over time, you’ll help us evolve our sales approach and shape the product by feeding insights and needs from the plant back to the product team, building the foundation for scaling across industries.

Your main responsibilities

  • Be the technical expert on sales calls and visits with cement plants.

  • Build trust with process engineers and plant teams by understanding their specific plant issues and linking them to how we can help.

  • Analyse plant data to identify and evaluate opportunities, then use this analysis to create compelling sales proposals.

  • Lead technical discovery and identify early when a plant does not meet our ICP (ideal customer profile) criteria.

  • Make sure relationships and plant understanding are handed over successfully to the deployment team.

  • Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that help shape our product roadmap.

  • Develop and iterate the pre-sales technical process, making it more impactful and more automated each time.

  • Travel to plants and conferences, around one week per month, to understand customer environments and explain the product.

What a great fit looks like

  • Exposure to physical sciences, controls, or heavy industry, such as cement, steel, energy, manufacturing, or similar.

  • Strong analytical skills and an outcome-oriented mindset. You can dig into industrial data, identify root causes, generate potential solutions, and explain their value in dollars and tonnes of CO2.

  • Excellent communication skills. You can build credibility and trust in complex industrial environments with both engineers and board-level stakeholders.

  • Comfortable being the technical voice in the conversation, presenting to senior plant leaders and operators, handling objections, and being challenged on your findings by people who have run kilns for 30 years.

  • Naturally curious and keen to learn about the industry, the technology, and each individual plant. You want to understand the root cause behind every question and objection so you can solve the right problem.

  • Confident in ambiguity and able to field very specific technical questions without getting flustered. You know when you can give your understanding, when you need to go and find the answer, and how to maintain customer confidence in both situations.

  • Willingness to travel regularly.

You’ll excel if

  • You build trust easily. You can connect with plant engineers, listen deeply, and align solutions to their priorities.

  • You’d rather diagnose than pitch. Your first instinct in a plant is to ask a better question, not to open the deck.

  • You thrive in dynamic environments. Fast-paced, ambiguous settings excite you, and you’re motivated by high-impact, mission-driven work.

  • You have experience working in heavy industry, particularly cement, steel, energy, heavy manufacturing, or similar.

Success in This Role Means

  • Plants say yes because the technical case is clear. You build customer confidence that Gigaton can deliver high ROI, helping us hit our revenue goals without losing deals because customers don’t understand or believe in our product and capabilities.

  • Deployments are set up to succeed. We haven’t overpromised to sign a contract, and our pre-contract analysis holds up once the system is live.

  • Process engineers trust and rely on you as a partner in solving problems.

  • Deals don’t stall waiting on a technical answer. Objections get handled quickly, and customers get the answers they need in good time.

    💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match.

    We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from all walks of life, with different countries, cultures, and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

    We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process

  1. Talent Partner Screen Call: Meet our talent partner and learn more about Gigaton and the role.

  2. Hiring Manager Screen: Meet our VP of Sales and discuss if this role is a good fit for you.

  3. Technical Onsite (completed on the same day):

    1. Technical interview

    2. Data analysis & presentation

  4. Operating Principles Interview: Understand how we work and whether Gigaton and you are a good fit for each other.

  5. Meet with the CEO: Every new potential hire meets Josh.

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty: Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership: High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun: Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

raw.description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Associate Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

What we're looking for

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

  • You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

  • You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

  • You're comfortable with data: you can write SQL or Python and answer your own questions

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Lendable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

  • Top-tier private health insurance

  • Offsites for the US Cards product and engineering team, and an annual whole-company trip abroad (previously Turkey and France)

Interview process

We respect your time and move quickly:

  1. Intro call (remote) - 30 minutes with the hiring manager

  2. Take-home exercise (remote) - a practical product challenge in your own time, followed by a video debrief with two members of the product team

  3. Final round (in our London office) - typically with the CPO and US Cards MD, Engineering Manager, Head of Product and hiring manager

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.
